svg.text: One breadboard, one ESP32. Use these pin names with your existing sketch.
Unplug USB before wiring. Large coloured dots mark wire endpoints; crossing wires do not connect.
Colour is a guide: always check D2, D4, D5, VIN and GND printed on your board.
Rows 31–63 below this section are unused.
Use one continuous rail section; bridge any rail break.
Wire to the printed pin names.
A–E connect in each numbered row.
Match the labels on YOUR module.
The pin order drawn is schematic.
Allow about 60 s for PIR warm-up.
1. Female jumper sockets go on ESP32 pins; male jumper ends go into breadboard holes.
2. Plug USB in, close Arduino Serial Monitor, then connect the USB port in Sensors & lights.
3. Press Full brightness. Then enable Buzzer and press Run test to check both outputs.
Keep the LED resistor in series. All grounds share the same blue rail section.
